title: Invalid regular expression.
summary: The regular expression cannot be parsed by the regexp package. Functions such as regexp.Compile return an error for this pattern, while regexp.MustCompile panics. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Invalid template.
summary: The Parse methods in text/template and html/template return an error for malformed template syntax, such as an unclosed action or an unexpected character in an action. Correct the template’s actions and delimiters before attempting to execute it. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Invalid format in time.Parse.
summary: time.Parse requires a layout string that uses Go’s reference time: Mon Jan 2 15:04:05 MST 2006. The layout must represent this date and time exactly. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Unsupported argument to functions in encoding/binary.
summary: The encoding/binary package can only serialize types with known sizes. This precludes the use of the int and uint types, as their sizes differ on different architectures. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Suspiciously small untyped constant in time.Sleep.
summary: The time.Sleep function takes a time.Duration as its only argument. Durations are expressed in nanoseconds. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Invalid first argument to exec.Command.
summary: os/exec runs programs directly (using variants of the fork and exec system calls on Unix systems). This shouldn’t be confused with running a command in a shell. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Printf with dynamic first argument and no further arguments.
summary: Using fmt.Printf with a dynamic first argument can lead to unexpected output. The first argument is a format string, where certain character combinations have special meaning. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Invalid URL in net/url.Parse.
summary: The URL contains a syntax error that causes net/url.Parse to return an error. Correct the URL’s syntax, using url.PathEscape or url.QueryEscape for individual path segments or query values that require escaping. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Non-canonical key in http.Header map.
summary: Keys in http.Header maps are canonical, meaning they follow a specific combination of uppercase and lowercase letters. Methods such as http.Header.Add and http.Header.Del convert inputs into this canonical form before manipulating the map. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: (*regexp.Regexp).FindAll called with n == 0, which will always return zero results.
summary: If n >= 0, the function returns at most n matches/submatches. To return all results, specify a negative number. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Various methods in the strings package expect valid UTF-8, but invalid input is provided.
summary: Functions in the strings package that process Unicode code points expect UTF-8-encoded strings. Invalid UTF-8 byte sequences are interpreted as Unicode replacement characters, not as the original bytes. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: A nil context.Context is being passed to a function, consider using context.TODO instead.
summary: The context package prohibits the use of a nil context. If no parent context is available, a new context should be used, e.g. context.TODO or context.Background. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Io.Seeker.Seek is being called with the whence constant as the first argument, but it should be the second.
summary: The first argument to Seek is a byte offset. The second argument selects the origin for that offset: io.SeekStart, io.SeekCurrent, or io.SeekEnd. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Non-pointer value passed to Unmarshal or Decode.
summary: Functions such as encoding/json.Unmarshal and (*encoding/json.Decoder).Decode require a pointer to the value that should be populated. Passing a non-pointer value results in the function returning an error at runtime, as it cannot modify the target value. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Using time.Tick in a way that will leak. Consider using time.NewTicker, and only use time.Tick in tests, commands and endless functions.
summary: Before Go 1.23, time.Tickers had to be closed to be able to be garbage collected. Since time.Tick doesn’t make it possible to close the underlying ticker, using it repeatedly would leak memory. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Trapping a signal that cannot be trapped.
summary: Not all signals can be intercepted by a process. Specifically, on UNIX-like systems, the syscall.SIGKILL and syscall.SIGSTOP signals are never passed to the process, but instead handled directly by the kernel. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Channels used with os/signal.Notify should be buffered.
summary: The os/signal package uses non-blocking channel sends when delivering signals. If the receiving end of the channel isn’t ready and the channel is either unbuffered or full, the signal will be dropped. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Strings.Replace called with n == 0, which does nothing.
summary: With n == 0, zero instances will be replaced. To replace all instances, use a negative number, or use strings.ReplaceAll. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Using a deprecated function, variable, constant or field.
summary: An API marked with a Deprecated: documentation comment is no longer recommended for use. Its deprecation message explains the reason and may suggest a replacement. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Using an invalid host:port pair with a net.Listen-related function.
summary: Functions such as net.Listen, net.ListenTCP, and similar, expect a valid network address in the form of host:port. The host, the port, or both, can be omitted, e.g. localhost:8080, :8080 or : are valid host:port pairs. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Using bytes.Equal to compare two net.IP.
summary: A net.IP stores an IPv4 or IPv6 address as a slice of bytes. The length of the slice for an IPv4 address, however, can be either 4 or 16 bytes long, using different ways of representing IPv4 addresses. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Modifying the buffer in an io.Writer implementation.
summary: Write must not modify the slice data, even temporarily. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: A string cutset contains duplicate characters.
summary: The strings.TrimLeft and strings.TrimRight functions take cutsets, not prefixes. A cutset is treated as a set of characters to remove from a string. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: It is not possible to use (*time.Timer).Reset’s return value correctly.
summary: When using pre-Go 1.23 timer semantics, draining a timer’s channel based on Reset’s return value is racy: the new timer may expire before the channel is drained, causing the new notification to be consumed instead of the old one. Stop the timer and, if necessary, drain its channel before calling Reset. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Cannot marshal channels or functions.
summary: JSON and XML encoders cannot represent values such as channels and functions, including those in exported struct fields or collection elements. XML encoding also does not support maps. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Atomic access to 64-bit variable must be 64-bit aligned.
summary: On ARM, x86-32, and 32-bit MIPS, it is the caller’s responsibility to arrange for 64-bit alignment of 64-bit words accessed atomically. The first word in a variable or in an allocated struct, array, or slice can be relied upon to be 64-bit aligned. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Sort.Slice can only be used on slices.
summary: The first argument of sort.Slice must be a slice. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Inappropriate key in call to context.WithValue.
summary: The provided key must be comparable and should not be of type string or any other built-in type to avoid collisions between packages using context. Users of WithValue should define their own types for keys. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Invalid argument in call to a strconv function.
summary: This check validates the format, number base and bit size arguments of the various parsing and formatting functions in strconv. It is in Staticcheck since 2021.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Overlapping byte slices passed to an encoder.
summary: In an encoding function of the form Encode(dst, src), dst and src were found to reference the same memory. This can result in src bytes being overwritten before they are read, when the encoder writes more than one byte per src byte. It is in Staticcheck since 2024.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Wrong order of arguments to errors.Is.
summary: The first argument of the function errors.Is is the error that we have and the second argument is the error we’re trying to match against. It is in Staticcheck since 2024.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: (*sync.WaitGroup).Add called inside the goroutine, leading to a race condition.
summary: (*sync.WaitGroup).Add must be called before starting the goroutine it is meant to wait for. Calling Add inside the goroutine creates a race condition between the call to Add and the call to Wait. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Empty critical section, did you mean to defer the unlock?.
summary: Empty critical sections of the kind. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Called testing.T.FailNow or SkipNow in a goroutine, which isn’t allowed.
summary: Methods such as FailNow and SkipNow, including Fatal, Fatalf, Skip, and Skipf, stop the calling goroutine using runtime.Goexit. They must be called from the goroutine running the test or benchmark, not from a goroutine it starts. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Deferred Lock right after locking, likely meant to defer Unlock instead.
summary: Deferring a call to Lock immediately after locking is almost always a typo. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: TestMain doesn’t call os.Exit, hiding test failures.
summary: Test executables (and in turn go test) exit with a non-zero status code if any tests failed. When specifying your own TestMain function, it is your responsibility to arrange for this, by calling os.Exit with the correct code. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Assigning to b.N in benchmarks distorts the results.
summary: The testing package dynamically sets b.N to improve the reliability of benchmarks and uses it in computations to determine the duration of a single operation. Benchmark code must not alter b.N as this would falsify results. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Binary operator has identical expressions on both sides.
summary: Using the same expression on both sides of an operator often indicates a copy-and-paste error or a typo. For example, x == x compares a value with itself, and x - x subtracts it from itself. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: &*x gets simplified to x, it does not copy x.
summary: Combining address-taking and pointer dereferencing does not create a copy of the pointed-to value. In particular, &*p still points to the same object as p. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Comparing unsigned values against negative values is pointless.
summary: An integer’s type limits the range of values it can hold. Comparisons against these limits can be redundant or indicate an incorrect boundary check. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: The loop exits unconditionally after one iteration.
summary: An unconditional break or return prevents a loop from running more than once, even if it appears to search or process multiple elements. Check whether the exit should depend on a condition, or whether a continue was intended. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Field assignment that will never be observed. Did you mean to use a pointer receiver?.
summary: A method with a value receiver operates on a copy of the receiver. Assigning to a field of that copy has no effect on the caller’s value. It is in Staticcheck since 2021.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: A value assigned to a variable is never read before being overwritten. Forgotten error check or dead code?.
summary: A value assigned to a variable may go unused even if the variable is read later, because a later assignment can overwrite the value first. This may hide a missing step, such as checking an error before reusing err. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: The variable in the loop condition never changes, are you incrementing the wrong variable?.
summary: It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: A function argument is overwritten before its first use.
summary: Overwriting a parameter before reading it discards the value supplied by the caller. This may indicate an accidental assignment or a parameter being used as a local variable. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: The result of append will never be observed anywhere.
summary: Calls to append produce a new slice value. When the result of append is assigned to a variable that is never subsequently read, the append operation may have an unintended effect. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Break statement with no effect. Did you mean to break out of an outer loop?.
summary: An unlabeled break terminates the innermost for, switch, or select statement. Inside a switch or select nested in a loop, it does not terminate the loop. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Comparing a value against NaN even though no value is equal to NaN.
summary: NaN is not equal to any value, including itself. Equality and ordering comparisons with NaN are always false, while != comparisons are always true. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Negating a boolean twice (!!b) is the same as writing b. This is either redundant, or a typo.
summary: Unlike languages that use double negation to convert a value to a boolean, Go only allows ! on boolean operands. Applying it twice restores the original value. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: An if/else if chain has repeated conditions and no side-effects; if the condition didn’t match the first time, it won’t match the second time, either.
summary: In an if/else if chain without side effects in its conditions, a repeated condition cannot become true after it was already false. The later branch is therefore unreachable. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Calling functions like math.Ceil on floats converted from integers doesn’t do anything useful.
summary: Converting an integer to a floating-point value does not produce a fractional part, NaN, or infinity. Applying math.Ceil, math.Floor, or math.Trunc to that value leaves it unchanged, and math.IsNaN and math.IsInf return false. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Certain bitwise operations, such as x ^ 0, do not do anything useful.
summary: The expressions x | 0 and x ^ 0 leave x unchanged, while x & 0 always produces zero. These operations may indicate a typo or an incorrectly defined bit mask. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Discarding the return values of a function without side effects, making the call pointless.
summary: Some functions return a result instead of modifying their arguments or other program state. Discarding all return values of such a function leaves its result unused. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Self-assignment of variables.
summary: Assigning a variable to itself preserves its existing value and is usually redundant. It may indicate a typo in either the source or the destination of an assignment, especially in a list of similar field assignments. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Multiple, identical build constraints in the same file.
summary: Multiple legacy +build lines are combined with a logical AND. Repeating the same constraint, even with its space-separated terms in a different order, does not further restrict when the file is built. Remove the duplicate line, or correct it if a different constraint was intended. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Unreachable case clause in a type switch.
summary: In a type switch like the following. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: X = append(y) is equivalent to x = y.
summary: Calling append with only a slice and no elements returns the slice unchanged. It does not copy its elements or allocate a new backing array. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Comparing the address of a variable against nil.
summary: Code such as if &x == nil is meaningless, because taking the address of a variable always yields a non-nil pointer. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Impossible comparison of interface value with untyped nil.
summary: Under the covers, interfaces are implemented as two elements, a type T and a value V. V is a concrete value such as an int, struct or pointer, never an interface itself, and has type T. For instance, if we store the int value 3 in an interface, the resulting interface value has, schematically, (T=int, V=3). It is in Staticcheck since 2020.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Checking for impossible return value from a builtin function.
summary: Return values of the len and cap builtins cannot be negative. It is in Staticcheck since 2021.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Integer division of literals that results in zero.
summary: When dividing two integer constants, the result will also be an integer. Thus, a division such as 2 / 3 results in 0. It is in Staticcheck since 2021.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Go constants cannot express negative zero.
summary: In IEEE 754 floating point math, zero has a sign and can be positive or negative. This can be useful in certain numerical code. It is in Staticcheck since 2021.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: (*net/url.URL).Query returns a copy, modifying it doesn’t change the URL.
summary: (*net/url.URL).Query parses the current value of net/url.URL.RawQuery and returns it as a map of type net/url.Values. Subsequent changes to this map will not affect the URL unless the map gets encoded and assigned to the URL’s RawQuery. It is in Staticcheck since 2021.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: X % 1 is always zero.
summary: The remainder of integer division by one is always zero, regardless of the dividend. If a remainder was intended, check whether the divisor should be a different value. It is in Staticcheck since 2022.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Ineffective attempt at sorting slice.
summary: sort.Float64Slice, sort.IntSlice, and sort.StringSlice are types, not functions. Doing x = sort.StringSlice(x) does nothing, especially not sort any values. It is in Staticcheck since 2022.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Ineffective attempt at generating random number.
summary: Functions in the math/rand package that accept upper limits, such as Intn, generate random numbers in the half-open interval [0,n). In other words, the generated numbers will be >= 0 and < n – they don’t include n. rand.Intn(1) therefore doesn’t generate 0 or 1, it always generates 0. It is in Staticcheck since 2022.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Checking never-nil value against nil.
summary: Values created by new or make, as well as function declarations and function literals, are non-nil. Checking such a value against nil cannot distinguish success from failure. It is in Staticcheck since 2022.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Comparing runtime.GOOS or runtime.GOARCH against impossible value.
summary: A file’s build constraints, including those implied by its name, limit the platforms on which its code can run. Comparing runtime.GOOS or runtime.GOARCH with a value excluded by those constraints makes an equality check always false and an inequality check always true. It is in Staticcheck since 2024.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Assignment to nil map.
summary: The zero value of a map is nil. Reading from a nil map is safe, but assigning to an element panics. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Deferring Close before checking for a possible error.
summary: If a call to acquire a resource fails, the returned resource may be nil or otherwise unusable. Deferring Close before handling the error can cause a panic instead of the intended error handling. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: The empty for loop (for {}) spins and can block the scheduler.
summary: An empty loop with no condition runs continuously, consuming CPU without doing useful work. An empty loop whose condition only reads ordinary variables cannot safely wait for another goroutine to change them: unsynchronized reads and writes constitute a data race. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Defers in infinite loops will never execute.
summary: Defers are scoped to the surrounding function, not the surrounding block. In a function that never returns, i.e. one containing an infinite loop, defers will never execute. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: For { select { ... with an empty default branch spins.
summary: A select with a default branch does not block when none of its channel operations can proceed. In an unconditional loop, an empty default branch therefore causes the loop to spin, consuming CPU while waiting for work. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: The finalizer references the finalized object, preventing garbage collection.
summary: A finalizer is a function associated with an object that runs when the garbage collector is ready to collect said object, that is when the object is no longer referenced by anything. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Infinite recursive call.
summary: A function that calls itself recursively needs to have an exit condition. Otherwise it will recurse forever, until the system runs out of memory. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Invalid struct tag.
summary: Malformed struct tags, duplicate keys, and invalid JSON or XML options can cause reflection-based packages to ignore the intended settings or report errors. Use the conventional space-separated key:"value" syntax and ensure that each option is supported by the package reading the tag and is appropriate for the field’s type. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Invalid Printf call.
summary: Formatting functions such as fmt.Printf and fmt.Sprintf require the format string to agree with the number and types of the arguments. Malformed formats, invalid argument indices, and mismatched arguments produce diagnostic text such as %!d(string=...) instead of the intended output. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Impossible type assertion.
summary: Some type assertions can be statically proven to be impossible. This is the case when the method sets of both arguments of the type assertion conflict with each other, for example by containing the same method with different signatures. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Passing odd-sized slice to function expecting even size.
summary: Some functions that take slices as parameters expect the slices to have an even number of elements. Often, these functions treat elements in a slice as pairs. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Using regexp.Match or related in a loop, should use regexp.Compile.
summary: The package-level functions regexp.Match, regexp.MatchString, and regexp.MatchReader compile the regular expression on every call. When the pattern is constant, calling these functions in a loop repeatedly performs the same compilation work. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Missing an optimization opportunity when indexing maps by byte slices.
summary: Map keys must be comparable, which precludes the use of byte slices. This usually leads to using string keys and converting byte slices to strings. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Storing non-pointer values in sync.Pool allocates memory.
summary: A sync.Pool is used to avoid unnecessary allocations and reduce the amount of work the garbage collector has to do. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Converting a string to a slice of runes before ranging over it.
summary: You may want to loop over the runes in a string. Instead of converting the string to a slice of runes and looping over that, you can loop over the string itself. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Inefficient string comparison with strings.ToLower or strings.ToUpper.
summary: Converting two strings to the same case and comparing them like so. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Using io.WriteString to write []byte.
summary: Using io.WriteString to write a slice of bytes, as in. It is in Staticcheck since 2024.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Defers in range loops may not run when you expect them to.
summary: Deferred calls run when the surrounding function returns, not at the end of each loop iteration. A range loop over a channel may keep receiving indefinitely if the channel is never closed, leaving deferred cleanup pending and allowing resources to accumulate. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Using a non-octal os.FileMode that looks like it was meant to be in octal.
summary: File permissions are conventionally written in octal, with one digit for each of the owner, group, and other permission sets. A literal such as 644 is decimal in Go and sets different permission bits than intended, potentially granting unwanted access. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Empty body in an if or else branch non-default.
summary: An empty branch often indicates missing code, such as an error that was checked but never handled. Implement the intended behavior, or simplify the conditional if the branch deliberately does nothing. It is in Staticcheck since 2017.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Only the first constant has an explicit type.
summary: In a constant declaration such as the following. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Trying to marshal a struct with no public fields nor custom marshaling.
summary: The encoding/json and encoding/xml packages only operate on exported fields in structs, not unexported ones. It is usually an error to try to (un)marshal structs that only consist of unexported fields. It is in Staticcheck since 2019.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Dubious bit shifting of a fixed size integer value.
summary: Bit shifting a value past its size will always clear the value. It is in Staticcheck since 2020.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Deleting a directory that shouldn’t be deleted.
summary: It is virtually never correct to delete system directories such as /tmp or the user’s home directory. However, it can be fairly easy to do by mistake, for example by mistakenly using os.TempDir instead of ioutil.TempDir, or by forgetting to add a suffix to the result of os.UserHomeDir. It is in Staticcheck since 2022.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Else branch of a type assertion is probably not reading the right value.
summary: When declaring variables as part of an if statement (like in if foo := ...; foo {), the same variables will also be in the scope of the else branch. This means that in the following example. It is in Staticcheck since 2022.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Ineffectual Go compiler directive.
summary: A potential Go compiler directive was found, but is ineffectual as it begins with whitespace. It is in Staticcheck since 2024.1. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.

title: Returned function should be called in defer.
summary: If you have a function such as. It is in Staticcheck since 2026.2. It is in the staticcheck group of checks.
